extracted.intended_audience: ICLR 2022 reviewers (assigned peer reviewers for the ICLR conference)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers on how to read, assess, discuss, and recommend decisions for ICLR 2022 submissions, including procedural duties, ethical obligations, review structure, and evaluation criteria. Intended to produce timely, substantive, and constructive reviews and to guide behavior during discussion and rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely and substantive reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Your reviews are timely and substantive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be submitted by the stated deadlines and contain enough detail and evidence to support the recommendation and help authors improve their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to reviewing guidelines and codes
rubrics_metrics.description: You follow the reviewing guidelines below. You adhere to our Code of Ethics in your role as a reviewer. You must also adhere to our Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report conflicts with the Code of Ethics (CoE) when present; follow behavioral and confidentiality standards laid out in the Code of Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create and maintain OpenReview/DBLP profiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Create your OpenReview profile and link your DBLP profile (by September 15th 2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep profile information up to date so conflicts of interest can be detected correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding on papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Bid on papers (7 October 2021 - 12 October 2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bidding to indicate preferences and conflicts; bid 'Very Low' for papers presenting a conflict of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging ethical or policy violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag any potential CoE violations and/or concerns (throughout the review and discussion phase).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate CoE violations when submitting the CoE report for the paper; contact AC/PC/ethics board as appropriate for resolution. For other violations (plagiarism, double submission, formatting), contact the AC or PC or post an official comment with appropriate readership restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the paper thoroughly and check related work
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the paper: It’s important to carefully read through the entire paper, and to look up any related work and citations that will help you comprehensively evaluate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give yourself sufficient time; consult related citations to judge novelty and placement in the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterize the objective of the work
rubrics_metrics.description: While reading, consider the following: Objective of the work: What is the goal of the paper? Is it to better address a known application or problem, draw attention to a new application or problem, or to introduce and/or explain a new theoretical finding?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different objectives require different considerations about potential value and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate strengths (clarity, correctness, rigor, reproducibility, novelty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong points: is the submission clear, technically correct, experimentally rigorous, reproducible, does it present novel findings (e.g. theoretically, algorithmically, etc.)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List and describe the concrete strengths; cite evidence from the paper (results, proofs, experiments) and note reproducibility aspects (clear algorithm, code, hyperparameters, datasets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Weak points: is it weak in any of the aspects listed in b.?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be comprehensive and specific about weaknesses (e.g., missing baselines, unclear exposition, incorrect derivation, insufficient experiments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid bias and be open-minded
rubrics_metrics.description: Be mindful of potential biases and try to be open-minded about the value and interest a paper can hold for the entire ICLR community, even if it may not be very interesting for you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let personal taste or narrow interests determine acceptance; consider broader community value and longer-term impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer the three key accept/reject questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer three key questions for yourself, to make a recommendation to Accept or Reject: (1) What is the specific question and/or problem tackled by the paper? (2) Is the approach well motivated, including being well-placed in the literature? (3) Does the paper support the claims? This includes determining if results, whether theoretical or empirical, are correct and if they are scientifically rigorous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these questions as the core of your assessment and to justify your overall recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a clear summary of the paper's claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize what the paper claims to contribute. Be positive and generous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a short, accurate summary at the start of your review so ACs and authors can immediately see your understanding of the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: List strong and weak points explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: List strong and weak points of the paper. Be as comprehensive as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize strengths and weaknesses as bullet points or numbered items to make the review easy to navigate and actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: State a clear recommendation with reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state your recommendation (accept or reject) with one or two key reasons for this choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give concise key reasons and then provide supporting arguments and evidence. Ensure the recommendation follows from the listed strengths and weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide supporting arguments and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide supporting arguments for your recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite specific experimental results, theoretical derivations, or comparisons to prior work that justify your judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask clarifying questions for authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask questions you would like answered by the authors to help you clarify your understanding of the paper and provide the additional evidence you need to be confident in your assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pose targeted, constructive questions that can be addressed in the rebuttal without requiring major new work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constructive feedback to improve the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide additional feedback with the aim to improve the paper. Make it clear that these points are here to help, and not necessarily part of your decision assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between feedback aimed at improving clarity or future work and the points that affect the accept/reject decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be polite, precise, and concrete
rubrics_metrics.description: Be polite in your review. Ask yourself whether you’d be happy to receive a review like the one you wrote. Be precise and concrete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid rude or dismissive language; provide concrete, actionable suggestions rather than vague criticism. Include references to back up claims about novelty or prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: State uncertainties explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: It’s also fine to explicitly state where you are uncertain and what you don’t quite understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate which points would be resolved by author responses or small clarifications, and which require stronger evidence or experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not reject solely for 'not interesting'
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t reject a paper just because you don’t find it 'interesting'. This should not be a criterion at all for accepting/rejecting a paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that value may be domain-specific or realized later; evaluate on scientific rigor, correctness, novelty, and potential impact to the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete the CoE report when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the CoE report: ICLR has adopted the Code of Ethics (CoE). Please check your assigned papers for conflicts with the code of ethics and mark them in your review form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If uncertain about a potential violation, reach out to your area chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage actively in discussion and rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in discussion: During the discussion phase, reviewers, authors and area chairs engage in asynchronous discussion, and authors are allowed to revise their submissions to address concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be responsive during this phase and able to reply to comments/requests within 3 business days; use discussion to resolve uncertainties and update your evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update final recommendation after discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide final recommendation: Update your review, taking into account the new information collected during the discussion phase, and any revisions to the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open to changing your initial recommendation either more positive or more negative based on rebuttal and discussion evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use supplementary material judiciously
rubrics_metrics.description: How should I use supplementary material? It is not necessary to read supplementary material but such material can often answer questions that arise while reading the main paper, so consider looking there before asking authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the main paper leaves important details to the supplement (e.g., proofs, hyperparameters), consult it to judge reproducibility and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request additional experiments only if justified and limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Am I allowed to ask for additional experiments? You can ask for additional experiments, but make sure you justify why they’re necessary to push the paper over the acceptance threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New experiments should not significantly change the content of the submission; they should be limited in scope and serve to more thoroughly validate existing results.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-of-the-art not required for acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission does not achieve state-of-the-art results, is that grounds for rejection? No, a lack of state-of-the-art results does not by itself constitute grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers can bring value by demonstrating new, relevant, impactful, or insightful knowledge even without SOTA performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations for citing recent work
rubrics_metrics.description: Are authors expected to cite and compare with very recent work? We consider papers contemporaneous if they are published (available in online proceedings) within the last four months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to cite relevant papers but may be excused for not knowing about very recent or non-peer-reviewed (arXiv-only) work; reviewers should use judgement and consult AC if in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid and report conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: How can I avoid being assigned papers that present a conflict of interest? Conflicts are detected using your OpenReview profile information (co-authors, past and current institutions, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update your OpenReview profile to avoid COIs; bid 'Very Low' for conflicted papers during bidding; if assigned a paper with a COI, contact program chairs immediately to reassign.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to contact area chair
rubrics_metrics.description: To contact the AC for a paper: (i) go to the OpenReview page for that paper (while being logged into OpenReview); (ii) click the button to add an official comment and fill out the comment form; (iii) add the ACs to the list of 'Readers'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use official OpenReview comments with appropriate readership restrictions for contacting area chairs about ethical/policy issues or clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and tone exemplars from review examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Example reviews show a well-structured format (summary, pros, cons, questions, minor comments, and post-rebuttal updates) and a constructive tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emulate clear organization (e.g., pros/cons lists), provide specific actionable requests (ablation suggestions, error corrections), and update decisions in post-rebuttal comments where appropriate.
